newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to monitor local offices of foreign banks.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to monitor local offices of foreign banks.

text.p: The Registrar of Banks said on Thursday he would begin monitoring the financial position of foreign banks' representatives offices in South Africa from March this year.
Christo Wiese said there were 60 representative offices in the country, some with substantial staff levels.
"We know some of them have 80 people...we want to start regulating them. Previously we've only licensed them or allowed them to operate, but there was no reporting requirement," he told Reuters.

Business Day newspaper said the move was likely to please local banks which have argued that the foreign representative offices had an unfair advantage because, unlike full branches, they did not have to comply with South Africa's regulatory requirements.
Wiese said he had asked for comments from foreign banks by the end of this month on suggested regulations and methods for submitting monthly returns.
Information to be submitted regularly under the proposals would include revenue earned, number of transactions, currency of loans and information on the size of operations.
